# FAQ-017 Engineering FAQ #17
Revision: Rev A

Q1: What torque should be used when tightening the blast wheel liner bolts on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why?
A1: Use 100 N·m for the blast wheel liner bolt torque on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01). Rationale: liners must be retained firmly to prevent movement under centrifugal loads while avoiding bolt yield. Over‑tightening risks stud fatigue and liner distortion; under‑tightening permits loosening and wear pattern escalation. Procedure: clean bolt threads, apply appropriate thread lubricant as specified in SOP-P2-L2-01, and tighten in a star pattern to 100 N·m using a calibrated torque wrench. Verification: record bolt locations and final torque in the maintenance log and retain the torque wrench calibration certificate with the job record. Related procedure: SOP-P2-L2-01 describes fastener handling and torque tool calibration. See SB-1002 for blast wheel assembly drawings.

Q2: What is the recommended lubrication interval for the main roll bearing on Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03), and what is the justification?
A2: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Rationale: rolling contact demands consistent grease replenishment to maintain film thickness and to displace contaminants; the interval is set to balance bearing life and maintenance downtime. Implementation: log machine run hours and perform lubrication at the 185 hours threshold using the grease grade specified in the equipment lubrication sheet. If a scheduled maintenance event coincides with the 185 hours mark, perform lubrication at that event. Records to keep: add an entry to the bearing lubrication log indicating equipment id EQ-P2-L2-RR03, date, run hours at service, grease batch/lot, and technician initials. Reference: confirm grease type and handling in SOP-P2-L2-04 and cross‑check bearing assembly notes in SB-1002.

Q3: How often should shot media be topped up in Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and how should the operation be documented?
A3: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Rationale: media attrition and segregation reduce blasting effectiveness; topping up at 40 hours maintains consistent media mass and surface treatment results. Practice: monitor media level visually or by the cabinet level indicator and add fresh media to restore the recommended fill as specified in SB-1002, ensuring media type and size match the job specification. Documentation: record media top-up events on the shot media log with equipment id EQ-P3-L2-SB01, media type, quantity added (use units per material handling form), operator initials, and any abnormal observations (e.g., fines, broken media). Include the media top-up entry in the process quality record for the part batch to maintain traceability per SOP-P2-L2-01.

Q4: What alarm setpoint should be used for the dust collector pressure drop on Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and what actions follow an alarm?
A4: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. Rationale: the setpoint reflects acceptable filter loading before performance degradation; an alarm at 1240 Pa indicates increased resistance and the need for inspection or service. Response steps: upon alarm, stop the blast cycle in a controlled manner, isolate the cabinet per SOP-P2-L2-04, and inspect filters and dust handling system for blockage, tears, or improper sealing. If filter change or cleaning is required, perform per SB-1002 filter replacement procedures and record the action. Records: log alarm time, equipment id EQ-P2-L1-SB03, observed pressure reading, corrective action taken, filter part identifiers (if changed), and technician name. Maintain the dust collector maintenance file and attach the alarm event log to the cabinet service record.

Q5: How long should spindle warm-up be allowed on Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) before precision work, and why is this necessary?
A5: The spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes. Rationale: thermal stabilization reduces spindle runout and thermal drift that would otherwise affect dimensional accuracy on precision parts. Procedure: run the spindle at low to moderate speed per the machine vendor recommendation during the 15 minutes warm-up period with no cutting load, then perform a test cut or calibration check before beginning production. Records: note warm-up time and confirmation of spindle checks in the machine log for EQ-P1-L4-CN01, including operator initials and any deviations observed. Reference SOP-P2-L2-04 for machine warm-up and verification steps and SB-1002 for machine capability notes.

Notes on records and traceability
- Always reference equipment id when entering logs (EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P2-L2-RR03, EQ-P2-L1-SB03, EQ-P1-L4-CN01).
- Maintain torque wrench calibration certificates and grease/ media lot information with each maintenance job record as specified in SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-04.
- Cross‑reference assembly and replacement details with SB-1002 where part interfaces or assemblies are involved.
- When any of the specified setpoints or intervals are exceeded or if abnormal conditions occur during service, attach a corrective action note to the equipment file and notify maintenance supervision per SOP-P2-L2-04.
